clue.text: Teatime conversation

parts.note: cha is an old slang word for tea, from Chinese

explanation.surface: A cosy natter over afternoon tea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Teatime' looks like one word setting the scene, but it splits into 'Tea' and 'time'.
explanation.definitionFit: A chat is an informal talk, a plain synonym for conversation.

clue.text: Officer in a tuxedo heartlessly upset worker

parts.note: a tuxedo is a dinner jacket, abbreviated DJ

indicators.note: heartlessly says the middle letters of the word upset are dropped, leaving its two ends

parts.note: the worker ant is the crossword's stock worker

explanation.surface: An officer in evening dress is somehow upsetting one of the staff.
explanation.walkthrough: DJ, short for dinner jacket, is the British name for a tuxedo. 'heartlessly' strips UPSET to its outer letters UT.
explanation.definitionFit: An adjutant is a military officer who assists a commanding officer with administration; it is also a stork.

clue.text: Gander to make noise like a chick

definitions.meaning: to take a gander is to have a quick look, a glance

definitions.text: to make noise like a chick
definitions.meaning: a chick's tiny high cheep is this sound

explanation.surface: A goose and a chick in the farmyard, each making a noise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gander' pretends to be the male goose; here it is the slang verb for a look.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses fit: a quick look, and the thin cry of a young bird.

clue.text: Mysterious coteries in disguise

indicators.note: something in disguise has its look changed, so the letters of coteries are rearranged

explanation.surface: Secretive cliques operating under cover.
explanation.definitionFit: Esoteric knowledge is understood only by a small initiated circle, so it is obscure or mysterious.

clue.text: Unoriginal commenter's standard twaddle

parts.note: par is the standard or normal level, as in golf
rot means nonsense, twaddle

explanation.surface: A critic who just repeats others usually talks nonsense.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who merely repeats what others say is said to imitate like a talking bird, so the bird names the copycat.

clue.text: One cuckoo — tailless cuckoo — finds way into Brazil?

parts.note: a nut is a crazy person, one who is cuckoo

indicators.note: tailless says the last letter is removed from the word that follows

parts.note: crackers is slang for mad, cuckoo

explanation.surface: A crazy bird somehow makes its way to South America.
explanation.walkthrough: Brazil is a Brazil nut, not the country; the question mark flags the definition by example.
explanation.definitionFit: A nutcracker is the tool that breaks open a hard shell such as a Brazil's; it is also a bird of the crow family.

clue.text: Queen observed king must eat crow

indicators.note: must eat says one piece swallows another, so it is placed inside

parts.note: observed means saw
K is the chess abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: A queen saw a king forced to eat humble pie, or a bird.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Eat crow' is a phrase for admitting error, but 'crow' alone is the definition, the verb to crow.
explanation.definitionFit: To crow is to give a loud harsh cry, which is what a squawk is.

clue.text: Opponent of conflict runs out of English port

indicators.note: runs out of a place says that letter leaves it, so it is removed

parts.note: Dover is the English Channel port
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A pacifist fleeing a Kentish port.
explanation.walkthrough: DOVER is the ferry port on the English Channel coast.
explanation.definitionFit: In politics a dove is someone who favours peace over war, the opposite of a hawk.

clue.text: Primarily horticultural border

indicators.note: primarily means take the first letter of the word horticultural

parts.note: an edge is a border

explanation.surface: A gardener's boundary in its simplest form.
explanation.definitionFit: A row of bushes planted as a boundary is first and foremost a garden boundary, so the whole clue describes it.

clue.text: Rock group standing round without question

indicators.note: without here means outside, so the round letter is placed on the outer edge of the question piece

parts.note: standing means status, position in society
O is round in shape

explanation.surface: A rock band hanging around without asking anything.
explanation.walkthrough: Status Quo is a long-running British rock band.
explanation.definitionFit: The band takes its name from the Latin phrase for the existing state of affairs.

clue.text: Musician from Thailand with funny Biblical rock

parts.note: T is Thailand's international vehicle registration letter
rum means odd or funny
Jesus called the apostle Peter the rock on which he would build his church

explanation.surface: A Thai musician playing amusing gospel rock.
explanation.definitionFit: A brass player who sounds a trumpet is a musician; it is also a bird.

clue.text: You may get a lift from this van in Rome — stick around!

definitions.text: You may get a lift from this

indicators.note: around says the stick piece encloses the other

parts.note: a cane is a walking stick

indicators.note: the van is the front, so this takes the first letter of Rome

explanation.surface: Hitching a lift in a van in Rome and told to wait about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'van' looks like a vehicle, fitting 'lift', but it means the front of Rome.
explanation.definitionFit: A crane is a machine that hoists heavy loads, giving them a lift.

clue.text: Undesirable correspondent in rock group plans for comeback

indicators.note: a comeback is a return, so the pieces are read backwards together

parts.note: R.E.M. is an American rock band
maps are plans or charts

explanation.surface: A rock band plotting a comeback has a fan who writes unwelcome letters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for comeback' turns REMMAPS round as a whole.
explanation.definitionFit: A sender of junk email is an unwanted correspondent.

clue.text: Short, fat person bowled instead of tail-ender in team

indicators.note: instead of says one letter replaces another, here the team's tail-ender, its last letter

parts.note: a squad is a team
B is the cricket abbreviation for bowled

explanation.surface: A stout cricketer bowled in place of the team's last batsman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tail-ender' is a cricket term for a weak late batsman; here it is the last letter D of SQUAD.
explanation.definitionFit: Squab as an adjective or noun describes someone short and plump; it is also a young pigeon.

clue.text: Philosopher espied larks about to get insects

parts.note: John Stuart Mill was an English philosopher

indicators.note: larks about means fools around, so the letters of espied are jumbled

explanation.surface: A philosopher spotted messing around and collecting bugs.
explanation.definitionFit: Millipedes are many-legged creepy-crawlies, loosely called insects though strictly they are not.

clue.text: Bad food queen swallows right for dog?

indicators.note: swallows says one piece is taken inside the other

parts.note: tack is poor-quality food, as in hardtack
ER is Elizabeth Regina, the Queen

explanation.surface: Is poor grub that a queen eats right for her dog?
explanation.walkthrough: 'dog' is the verb, to follow; the question mark marks the loose fit.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who dogs another follows their trail closely, as a trailing pursuer does.

clue.text: Old magistrate to turn up with heart of steel

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the word is written from bottom to top, reversed

parts.note: to veer is to turn

indicators.note: the heart is the central letter of the word steel

explanation.surface: A judge of old showing courage with a heart of steel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to turn up' looks like 'arrive', but splits into 'turn' (VEER) and 'up', its reversal.
explanation.definitionFit: A reeve was a local official or magistrate in medieval England; it is also a female ruff, a bird.

clue.text: Up to no good, luting merrily

indicators.note: merrily suggests playing around, so the remaining letters are shuffled
no good says the letter for good is taken away

explanation.surface: Someone up to mischief, cheerfully playing the lute.
explanation.walkthrough: 'no good' removes G from LUTING, leaving LUTIN, which 'merrily' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: Until is a preposition meaning up to a given time.

clue.text: Jazz fan chants unevenly

indicators.note: unevenly says take the odd-numbered letters of the word chants

explanation.surface: A jazz lover singing out of rhythm.
explanation.definitionFit: In old jazz slang a cat is an enthusiast or hip musician.

clue.text: What performer doesn't want to get lead in Scorsese film?

parts.words: What performer doesn't want to get
parts.note: to get the bird is to be booed or hissed by an audience

indicators.note: the lead of a word is its first letter, here of Scorsese

explanation.surface: An actor hoping for a lead role in a Scorsese picture.
explanation.walkthrough: The film is Hitchcock's, not Scorsese's; Scorsese only supplies its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: The Birds is Hitchcock's 1963 thriller about avian attacks, a famous film.

clue.text: Bowie, say, printing material backing heavy metal

indicators.note: backing means going backwards, so the word is reversed

parts.note: ink is what printers use
Fe is the chemical symbol for iron

explanation.surface: David Bowie printed on merchandise for a heavy metal band.
explanation.walkthrough: Bowie is the Bowie blade, not the singer.
explanation.definitionFit: A Bowie is a large hunting blade named after Jim Bowie, an example of the cutting tool.

clue.text: My! Tories messing up a form of equality

indicators.note: messing up means jumbling, so the letters of my and tories are rearranged

explanation.surface: Exclaiming at Conservatives botching their policy on fairness.
explanation.walkthrough: Tories are members of Britain's Conservative Party.
explanation.definitionFit: In geometry an isometry is a mapping that keeps distances unchanged, a kind of equal measure.

clue.text: Streamers in Cork to welcome loon back

indicators.note: to welcome is to take in, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a bung is a cork or stopper

indicators.note: back says the word is reversed

parts.note: a nit is a fool, a loon

explanation.surface: Decorations in Cork to greet a returning eccentric.
explanation.walkthrough: Cork looks like the Irish city; it is the stopper. 'back' turns NIT to TIN.
explanation.definitionFit: Bunting is strings of little flags hung as decoration; it is also a bird.

clue.text: Scot from the South notices Greek maidens

indicators.note: in a down clue reading from the south means bottom to top, reversed

parts.note: Ian is a typical Scottish name
ads are notices or advertisements

explanation.surface: A Scotsman from down south spots some Greek girls.
explanation.definitionFit: Naiads are water nymphs of Greek mythology, female spirits of springs and rivers.

clue.text: Government to incite complaint

parts.note: to rouse is to stir up or incite

explanation.surface: The state stirring up grievances.
explanation.definitionFit: A grouse is a grumble or complaint; it is also a game bird.

clue.text: Fleshy part of nobleman with honour

parts.note: an earl is a British nobleman
the OBE, Order of the British Empire, is a British honour

explanation.surface: A soft spot of an aristocrat with a decoration.
explanation.walkthrough: An OBE is an honour awarded by the British monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: The soft lobe at the bottom of the outer ear is a small fleshy piece.

clue.text: What knockers do, given pinch in tops of satiny elastic

indicators.note: in says the pinch piece sits inside the two first letters
tops of takes the first letter of each of satiny and elastic

parts.note: to nip is to pinch

explanation.surface: A saucy picture of a bra's satin elastic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'knockers' here are critics, people who knock others.
explanation.definitionFit: To snipe is to make sly critical attacks, which is what detractors do.

clue.text: Aussie runner's small and pale

parts.note: wan means pale

explanation.surface: An Australian athlete who is short and pallid.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'runner' in crosswords is often a river; the Swan flows through Perth in Western Australia.
explanation.definitionFit: The Swan River runs through Perth, so it is an Australian flowing watercourse; also a bird.

clue.text: Two ducks with nice leg cooked in ancient period

indicators.note: cooked means prepared or altered, so these letters are mixed together

parts.note: a duck is a zero score in cricket, shaped like O, so two give OO

explanation.surface: A recipe for a pair of ducks with a nice leg, cooked long ago.
explanation.definitionFit: The Oligocene is a geological epoch of about 34 to 23 million years ago.

clue.text: WWI enemy destroying British missile launch site

indicators.note: destroying the letter for British means it is wiped out of the word

parts.note: Boche was a derogatory term for German soldiers

explanation.surface: A German attacking a British rocket base in the Great War.
explanation.walkthrough: The oche is the line darts players throw from; darts are the missiles.
explanation.definitionFit: The oche is where a darts player stands to throw, launching small arrows at the board.

clue.text: Irish flower found through the internet

indicators.note: found through says the letters sit inside, spanning the words the internet

explanation.surface: An Irish bloom discovered online.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'flower' is something that flows: a river, here the Erne in Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: The Erne is a river in Ireland, a thing that flows; it is also a sea eagle.

clue.text: Sent more compasses about ship

indicators.note: to compass is to encircle, so one piece goes around the others

parts.note: added means extra, more
re means about or concerning
SS is steamship

explanation.surface: Sending extra navigation instruments by sea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'compasses' looks like navigation tools; it is the verb to surround.
explanation.definitionFit: A letter addressed to someone is directed or sent to them.

clue.text: Newton follows star Greek mathematician

indicators.note: follows puts the Newton letter after the star piece

parts.note: a hero is a star, a celebrated figure
N is the abbreviation for newton, the unit of force

explanation.surface: Isaac Newton coming after a great ancient mathematician.
explanation.walkthrough: Newton suggests the scientist but supplies only N, the unit symbol.
explanation.definitionFit: Heron of Alexandria was a first-century Greek mathematician and engineer; it is also a wading bird.
